summary:
MISSION PULSE (by Team AstroAlert) is a live, offline-first astronaut health state-awareness and guided self-assessment web application for long-duration space missions (https://mission-pulse-hz8r.vercel.app/). During deep-space travel, variable Earth–Mars communication delays and the five NASA spaceflight hazards (radiation, altered gravity, isolation, distance, and closed environments) mean crew members must notice and verify health changes autonomously with constrained onboard equipment.

Instead of using rigid Earth clinical cutoffs that cause false alarms, MISSION PULSE calibrates each astronaut's personal baseline (Median ± 2×MAD) across six indicators: resting heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, core temperature, sleep duration, and radiation (mGy/d). Our engine filters out post-exercise spikes (Day 19: 142 bpm) and loose-sensor faults (Day 44: 205 bpm), freezes the baseline on Day 26 against drift contamination, and flags true 3-of-4 day persistent drift (Day 30: 69 bpm, 5.5h sleep) on an interactive Anatomical X-Ray Twin. It guides astronauts through non-diagnostic 2-minute verification checks, a 10×10 SANS Amsler grid, and offline store-and-forward summaries for ground medical teams—reducing alarm fatigue in space and remote Earth healthcare.
details:
LIVE WEB APPLICATION & OPEN-SOURCE REPOSITORY

• Live Spacecraft Console Demo: https://mission-pulse-hz8r.vercel.app/

• Public GitHub Repository (MIT License): https://github.com/swanthalok-stack/Mission-Pulse

• 7-Slide Presentation Deck: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1U_T1mLV0TOBZ3zNeVh4RFM-UXvizmDR4/view

• Team AstroAlert Members: Agnes, Esha, Swanth, and Sevinch

1. WHAT DOES IT DO AND HOW DOES IT WORK?

MISSION PULSE is an offline-first, non-diagnostic astronaut health state-awareness and guided self-assessment web application designed for long-duration lunar (Artemis) and Mars missions.

• 6-Indicator Live Telemetry & Hardware Layer: Tracks Resting Heart Rate (bpm), Blood Pressure (mmHg), Blood Glucose (mg/dL), Core Body Temperature (°C), Sleep Duration (h), and Environmental Radiation (mGy/d via simulated Canadian Space Agency CANS & Radi-N2 dosimetry), alongside manual crew check-ins and 60-day CSV import/export.

• 4-Stage Non-Parametric Personal Baseline Engine:

- Stage 1 (Confounder Gate): Automatically filters out expected physiological spikes from logged ARED resistance exercise (Day 19: 142 bpm), post-meal glucose peaks (Day 16: 138 mg/dL), and hardware optical PPG sensor faults (<50% signal quality on Day 44: 205 bpm).

- Stage 2 (Individual Calibration): Establishes each astronaut's personal reference band across Mission Days 1–14 using non-parametric statistics: Median ± max(2 × MAD, V_floor).

- Stage 3 (Day 26 Anti-Contamination Baseline Freeze): Automatically freezes the reference baseline on Day 26 ("BASELINE FROZEN @ DAY 26") the moment consecutive drift begins so gradual physiological deterioration cannot corrupt the normal band.

- Stage 4 (Explainable 3-of-4 Day Persistence Flag): Flags sustained multi-day drift (Days 27–30: Resting HR climbing 63 -> 65 -> 67 -> 69 bpm alongside 5.5h sleep debt) and displays a transparent counterfactual rule trace explaining why the alert triggered.

• Guided Non-Physician Self-Assessment & SANS Lab: When a persistent drift flag triggers, the crew member is guided through a 2-minute verification workflow (5 step-by-step clinical protocols with hands-free audio instructions), an interactive 10×10 Digital Amsler Grid for Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) visual distortion tracking, and a Day 50 (2.80 mGy/d) Solar Particle Event storm-shelter checklist.

• Offline Store-and-Forward Flight Surgeon Sync: Packages verified telemetry and check-in summaries with SHA-256 integrity hashes for asynchronous transmission across simulated ISS (2s), Lunar (1.3s), and Mars (up to 22 min) One-Way Light-Time (OWLT) delays.

2. WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE & WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT?

• For Deep-Space Astronauts: Eliminates alarm fatigue from exercise/sensor spikes while catching subtle multi-day physiological drift during communication blackouts when Earth flight surgeons cannot respond in real time.

• For Ground Medical Teams (Flight Surgeons): Delivers structured, context-tagged, high-signal verification summaries instead of noisy raw wearable streams.

• For Earth Healthcare (CSA Space-to-Earth Impact): Directly translates to rural and remote Earth telemedicine, elderly aging-in-place longitudinal monitoring, and wearable false-alarm reduction by comparing individuals against their own personal baseline rather than rigid population averages.

3. HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

• Anti-Contamination Baseline Freeze (Day 26): Standard rolling averages slowly absorb multi-day health drift and mask illness; our engine detects nascent drift and locks the clean calibration window.

• Calm-by-Default Anatomical X-Ray Twin: Projects organ-specific anomaly beacons onto an interactive anatomical twin only during verified drift or confounder events, remaining 100% calm (zero blinking dots) on all nominal days.

• Ethical Non-Punitive Crew Stewardship & Privacy Enclave: Replaces punitive readiness scores with supportive daily habit rings and protects crew psychological notes inside a role-based privacy enclave ([REDACTED — CREW PRIVATE ENCLAVE] in Flight Surgeon view) so astronauts never hide symptoms out of fear of mission grounding.

4. WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, OR SOFTWARE DID YOU USE?

• Frontend & Core Engine: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 SVG Spline Charts, Lucide React Icons, and Browser LocalStorage (100% offline-capable persistence).

• Audio & Accessibility: Native Browser Web Speech API (SpeechSynthesis & SpeechRecognition) for hands-free eyes-busy crew operation, plus WCAG high-contrast redundant iconography.

• Simulated Hardware Streams: Modeled on Artemis II optical wrist actigraphy, oscillometric brachial blood pressure cuffs, and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) CANS / Radi-N2 radiation dosimeters.

• Testing & Deployment: Node.js & Puppeteer automated 16-module verification suites (verify-all-16-modules.cjs, verify-regressions.cjs), Git/GitHub, Canva (7-slide deck), and Vercel production hosting.

5. WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?

• Variable Earth–Mars Communication Delays (OWLT up to 22 minutes + solar conjunction blackouts requiring 100% Earth-independent operation).

• NASA's 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight (RIDGE: Space Radiation, Isolation & Confinement, Distance from Earth, Gravity Fields, and Hostile/Closed Environments per NASA-STD-3001).

• Non-Physician Usability & Clinical Safety: All outputs are strictly informational and non-diagnostic, empowering crew state-awareness without replacing professional medical judgment.

6. SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) & AI TOOLS TRANSPARENCY DISCLOSURE

In compliance with NASA Space Apps Challenge Super Intelligence (SI) guidelines, Team AstroAlert discloses all SI tools utilized and confirms that NO generated content contains, uses, or modifies any NASA branding, logos, flags, or official mission identifiers:

- Code, Mathematics & Research Synthesis: Google Gemini and Antigravity 2.0 (SI-assisted IDE) were used to synthesize publicly available NASA HRP and CSA reference guidelines, verify our non-parametric baseline equations (Median ± 2×MAD), accelerate React 19 + TypeScript UI styling, and build automated Puppeteer regression tests. All physiological anomaly detection rules, confounder gates, and 3-of-4 day drift calculations are 100% deterministic TypeScript functions.

- Images & Visual Assets: The dark-mode anatomical X-Ray silhouette (/public/xray-body.png) in the X-Ray Twin panel was generated using an SI image generation model, contains zero NASA logos or insignia, and carries a visible on-screen watermark badge ("SI-Generated Graphic") alongside metadata acknowledgement.

- Audio & In-App Companion: Hands-free voice readout is synthesized via the browser's native Web Speech API (SpeechSynthesis) and acknowledged in UI descriptive text and metadata. The in-app "Pulse AI" companion operates strictly as an offline-capable, read-only local Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) explainer over deterministic rule-trace telemetry and official NASA HRP / CSA citations—no generative model ever invents clinical thresholds or issues medical diagnoses.
